summary: In Greek mythology, Antiphates (Ancient Greek Ἀντιφάτης) is a name shared by several men. The atlas node antiphates-melampid is the Melampodid of Argos — son of Melampus and Iphianeira, husband of Zeuxippe, father of Oicles — the genealogical link between the healing house of Melampus and the seer Amphiaraus destroyed at Thebes.

sections.heading: Son of Melampus
paragraphs: Apollodorus records Antiphates as son of Melampus by Iphianeira daughter of Megapenthes. By Zeuxippe daughter of Hippocoon he fathers Oicles (and, in some notices, Amphalces); Oicles in turn begets Amphiaraus, carrying the Melampodid gift of prophecy into the generation of the Seven.

Homonym care: not Antiphates king of the Laestrygonians who eats Odysseus' scouts; not the Greek in the Trojan Horse; not the Trojan slain by Leonteus; not Sarpedon's son in the Aeneid. The atlas id is the Argive Melampodid alone.
